## Purpose

Support HiSparse for single-engine Qwen3.8-Flash QSA, whose full K/V heads differ from sparse MLA geometry. QSA can read selected history after its GPU pages are reclaimed, using the existing resident/hot/host policy.

The indexer's selection budget, logical positions and valid counts are preserved. Indexer caches, raw-key rings and recurrent state stay on GPU; no additional attention approximation is introduced.

## Changes

- Add full-row QSA geometry, BLNHC layout, TP ownership and host accounting.
- Connect writes and selected reads to residency/refill, including nonresident prefill and independent BF16/FP8 main and indexer formats.
- Preserve MTP selection reuse with stable selected-K/V storage and a private padding request map for native FULL replay and async execution.
- Preserve writable ownership across partial prefix hits, recompute, cancellation and cleanup.

NIXL/P-D and DCP are outside this PR.

## Usage

Initial eager TP2 example with a compatible checkpoint:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$QSA_MODEL" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"bf16","hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":8}}'
```

Keep the hybrid cache manager enabled. Host capacity is logical per DP replica; physical allocation depends on TP ownership/alignment. 

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py
```

Coverage includes TP ownership, BF16/FP8 main and indexer formats, refill after page reuse, MTP selection reuse, CUDA graph replay, prefix reuse and cleanup. Targeted regressions, lint and mypy passed. A three-request startup check with TP2, MTP3, FULL_DECODE_ONLY and async scheduling passed, followed by graceful shutdown. The latest main synchronization passed 65 targeted CPU regression cases, lint and mypy. GPU startup and model tests were not rerun after this synchronization.

**GSM8K: 197/200 with HiSparse off and 197/200 on**, with no question-level gains or losses. This 200-question subset includes one HiSparse-on response that reached the 4096-token limit and remained scored incorrect. 

## Preliminary performance

### Finite-wave benchmark

![Output throughput versus per-user token speed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c353faa0-673b-4df4-8ddb-4edf317256a4)

Each plotted point is one complete off/on pair with N=C requests; * marks a paired retry. Per-user speed is `1000 / mean TPOT(ms)`. Three additional paired repeats at the concurrency with the highest observed throughput in either mode give the following medians [min, max]:

| Input/output tokens | C | Off output tok/s | On output tok/s | Change | Mean TPOT off/on (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20,000/10,000 | 64 | 4846.42 [4813.67, 4882.21] | 3838.20 [3819.87, 3888.61] | −20.80% | 11.954 / 15.070 |
| 32,000/8,000 | 128 | 3233.18 [3218.93, 3246.51] | 3651.65 [3608.98, 3741.73] | +12.94% | 14.809 / 28.302 |
| 60,000/10,000 | 32 | 2585.73 [2564.60, 2589.29] | 2074.85 [2049.17, 2078.34] | −19.76% | 10.471 / 13.062 |

### AIPerf

AIPerf 0.13.0 maintains client concurrency for 600 seconds, then drains requests. Each point is one preliminary run with exactly 32,000 input and 8,000 output tokens per request. Off/on therefore complete different request totals. Aggregate throughput includes drain; mean tok/s/user averages per-request reciprocal ITL, unlike the finite-wave chart's reciprocal mean TPOT.

| C | Requests off/on | Output tok/s off/on | Change | Mean tok/s/user off/on |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 224 / 192 | 2926.49 / 2407.26 | −17.74% | 96.06 / 79.18 |
| 64 | 298 / 256 | 3482.59 / 3142.21 | −9.77% | 65.30 / 53.05 |
| 128 | 362 / 303 | 3490.70 / 3413.72 | −2.21% | 65.51 / 35.56 |
| 256 | 490 / 429 | 3541.53 / 3354.45 | −5.28% | 64.81 / 31.42 |

All reported measurements completed with zero request errors and full input/output lengths. Finite waves show a workload-dependent throughput/latency tradeoff; **AIPerf did not show a throughput gain**. Neither establishes gains at the default GPU KV budget or a maximum supported concurrency.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark configuration</summary>

Both modes use TP2 on a GB300-provisioned machine (device-reported NVIDIA L20B, 284,208 MiB/GPU), NVFP4 weights, BF16 main/index KV, FP32 SSM and BF16 pinned-CPU PLE on both ranks. GPU KV is 32 GiB/rank; HiSparse hot capacity is 4096 rows and the indexer budget stays 2048. Requested and resolved `async-scheduling` are enabled, with FULL_DECODE_ONLY, MTP off, prefix caching off and chunked prefill on. Maximum context/batched tokens: 70,000/8192. Streaming completions use temperature 0, seed 42 and `ignore_eos`.

| Parameter | Finite wave | AIPerf |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client | vLLM bench | AIPerf 0.13.0 |
| Logical host pool / max sequences | 128 GiB / 128 | 256 GiB / 256 |
| Graph capture sizes | Powers of two, 1–128 | Powers of two, 1–256 |
| Workload | Three profiles above; N=C | 32k/8k; C=32,64,128,256; 600 s issuance, up to 900 s drain |
| Warmup | Separate 1024-input/32-output requests | C full-profile requests, excluded from measurement |

The paired GPU byte budgets match, but startup hybrid-group capacity estimates differ: 2,349,200 tokens off versus 2,273,034 on. These are not measured admission ceilings. Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Torch compile mode 0; FA2 fallback warnings were observed. The short finite-wave warmup may include lazy compilation in measured timings. Validation used prebuilt native extensions and does not establish a clean build with all dependency constraints satisfied.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Latency, resource and transfer observations</summary>

AIPerf values below are off/on. Running includes prefill; client concurrency is not active decode concurrency. Gauge maxima are sampled within the profiling window, including drain and excluding warmup.

| C | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean TTFT (s) | GPU KV peak (%) | Running max | Waiting max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 10.425 / 12.653 | 3.978 / 4.986 | 59.153 / 56.230 | 32 / 32 | 27 / 26 |
| 64 | 15.633 / 19.186 | 12.443 / 8.313 | 100 / 89.976 | 64 / 64 | 54 / 57 |
| 128 | 15.717 / 31.001 | 129.610 / 23.027 | 100 / 90.107 | 64 / 128 | 114 / 117 |
| 256 | 15.821 / 44.261 | 327.593 / 187.167 | 100 / 99.944 | 64 / 179 | 230 / 233 |

HiSparse counters use before/after differences with warmup excluded. C64 retains bounds because scrapes bracket the measurement boundaries.

| AIPerf C | Hot hits Δ | Hot misses Δ | H2D bytes Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 64 | 3,995,482,608–4,205,948,228 | 996,515,588–1,051,866,060 | 1,020,431,962,112–1,077,110,845,440 |
| 128 | 25,956,632,668 | 7,213,988,280 | 7,387,123,998,720 |
| 256 | 66,981,513,952 | 16,658,652,692 | 17,058,460,356,608 |

Host→hot refill was observed at AIPerf C64/128/256, and was not observed at C32. For the three finite-wave repeat groups above, miss/H2D deltas were zero for 20k/10k C64 and 60k/10k C32, and positive for 32k/8k C128. Off-mode transfer counters are unavailable. Full-window D2H counts and GPU VRAM peaks are unavailable for both protocols; strict-window finite-wave KV peaks and running/waiting counts cannot be reconstructed. Missing metrics are not zero, and no residency mode is inferred from zero counters.

</details>

**Low-concurrency overhead remains unresolved.** Slowdowns occur without observed hot misses/H2D. The enabled path still performs location resolution, gather launches, index copies, stream ordering and eager host mirroring. In a separate single-run, fixed-work C32 comparison, disabling mirroring improved throughput by 2.14% but remained 16.59% below off; a BMM variant also changed, so the gap cannot be attributed entirely to mirroring or refill.

## Review

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and documentation; human line-by-line review and submitter validation are pending.

The prior upstream search found no equivalent full-head QSA adaptation; [DeepSeek V4 HiSparse support](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53592) uses sparse-MLA geometry.

+## QSA models
+
+For Qwen4Exp QSA models, configuring `HiSparseConnector` enables main K/V
+offloading and selects Model Runner V2:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve QSA_MODEL \
+  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":8}}'
+```
+
+The device layout resolves to `BLNHC`, so one copy row holds a token's K and V
+for every local K/V head. Compressed indexer keys, raw-key rings and recurrent
+state stay GPU-resident. With prefix caching, prefixes are reused at whole
+scheduler-page boundaries; matching tokens past the boundary are recomputed.
+P/D disaggregation and decode context parallelism are not supported for QSA.

+    row_width = num_kv_heads * 2 * head_dim

+    fp8 = cache_dtype != torch.bfloat16
+    storage_dtype = torch.uint8 if fp8 else torch.bfloat16
+    k_scale, v_scale = (0.5, 2.0) if fp8 else (1.0, 1.0)
+    backing = torch.full(
+        (num_blocks * block_stride,), 7, device="cuda", dtype=storage_dtype
+    )
+    view = PagedCacheView.bind(
+        backing.view(torch.uint8),
+        dtype=backing.dtype,
+        row_width=row_width,
+        byte_offset=block_size * row_width * backing.element_size(),
+        block_stride=block_stride * backing.element_size(),
+        num_blocks=num_blocks,
+        block_size=block_size,
+    )
+    original = torch.randn(

+        original_value = (original_value.float() / v_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    stored = torch.cat(
